title_ar: الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يحاضر  لجمعية المرأة عن:"نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم".
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Lectures to the Women's Association on "Supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace"
body_ar:
الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو يحاضر لجمعية المرأة عن:"نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم".

ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء محاضرة بعنوان: "نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم"

في معهد بن عباس وسط العاصمة انواكشوط، مساء يوم أمس الاثنين الموافق لــ 04-07-2011 وهي محاضرة تأتي ضمن برنامج المخيم النسوي الذي تقيمه جمعية المرأة للتربية والثقافة بمباني المعهد، وقد تطرق الشيخ في هذه المحاضرة لشمائل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومواقف مؤثرة من نُصرة الصحابة رضوان الله عليهم له، وذكر أنه على قدر محبتنا له وتعظيمنا للدين الحنيف الذي أتى به تكون نصرته ومستوى التضحية في سبيل إعلاء كلمة الله تعالى، نذكر من ذلك تلخيصا ما يلي:

• أختار الله سبحانه وتعالى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم لرسالته اختيارا سابقا لخلقته واصطفاه من بين الأنبياء لرسالته وخصه بالإسراء والمعراج ورفعه مكانا عليا عند سدرة المنتهى .

• وشرفه من بين الخلائق بالشفاعة العظمى التى اعتذر عنها الأنبياء أولو العزم من الرسل وقال له " اشفع تشفع واسأل تعط.."، وخصه الله كذلك بالوسيلة وهي درجة في الجنة لا تنبغي إلا لرجل واحد وهو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم .

• وخصه بأن جعله شهيدا على الخلائق أجمعين فالرسل هم شهداء الله على الناس، والرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم شهيد عليهم أجمعين، ومن شرط هذه الشهادة العلم بالشرع والتفقه في الدين.

• وشرفه بأن جعله أكثر الرسل تابعا يوم القيامة؛ فقد عُرض عليه الأنبياء يوم القيامة فكان يرى النبي ومعه الرهط، والنبي ومعه الرهيط، والنبي ومعه الرجل، والنبي ومعه الرجلان، والنبي وليس معه أحد، حتى رأى سوادا عظيما فقال هذه أمتي فقيل هذا موسى وأمته، ولكن انظر إلى الأفق فنظر فإذا سواد عظيم قد سد الأفق فقيل هذه أمتك ومعهم سبعون ألفا يدخلون الجنة بغير حساب ولا عذاب .

• وشرفه يوم القيامة باللواء المعقود له يوم القيامة؛ في يمينه لواء الحمد يرفعه وتحت هذا اللواء يدخل الأنبياء وأممهم والصالحون من كل أمة وتأتي أمته غرا محجلين يعرفهم من بين الأمم فيدعون باسمه، " يَوْمَ نَدْعُو كُلَّ أُنَاسٍ بِإِمَامِهِمْ فَمَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ فَأُوْلَئِكَ يَقْرَءُونَ كِتَابَهُمْ وَلا يُظْلَمُونَ فَتِيلاً (71)(الإسراء).

• وشرفه كذلك بأن ختم به الرسالة إلى أهل الأرض إيذانا بأن الدين الحق هو ما جاء به محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، فكل الأديان الأخرى كانت إعدادا لهذا الدين الكامل.

• وشرفه كذلك بأن جعل أمته خير أمة أخرجت للناس؛ (وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً لِتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيداً)(من الآية 142 من سورة البقرة).

• وشرفه بأن جعل علماء أمته كأنبياء بني إسرائيل في المنزلة، فإن بني إسرائيل كانت تسوسهم الأنبياء، فجعل الله العلماء ورثته فهم يسوسون أمته كما كانت الأنبياء تسوس بني إسرائيل، وقد تعهد الله له بأن يبعث على رأس كل مئة سنة من هذه الأمة من يجدد لها أمر دينها.

• وكذلك شرفه بأن رفع الحرج عن أمته جملة وتفصيلا؛ فقال تعالى: (وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمْ الْمُسْلِمينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ)(من الآية 78 من سورة الحج).

• الله سبحانه وتعالى لما دعانا لنصرة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ضرب لنا المثل بالحواريين لما بعث الله عيسى فدعاهم إلى نصرته فانقسم بنو إسرائيل إلى فرقتين وطائفتين بين مصدقين لعيسى ومكذبين له فقال الله تعالى:( يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا كُونوا أَنصَارَ اللَّهِ كَمَا قَالَ عِيسَى ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ لِلْحَوَارِيِّينَ مَنْ أَنصَارِي إِلَى اللَّهِ قَالَ الْحَوَارِيُّونَ نَحْنُ أَنصَارُ اللَّهِ فَآَمَنَتْ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ وَكَفَرَتْ طَائِفَةٌ فَأَيَّدْنَا الَّذِينَ آَمَنُوا عَلَى عَدُوِّهِمْ فَأَصْبَحُوا ظَاهِرِينَ) (14)(سورة الصف).

• من المواقف المؤثرة في زمن الصحابة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما رجع من غزوة أحد واستقبله الناس بمسجد المستراح رأى امرأة يصدها الرجال عنه فقال دعوها فقد قتل بين يديّ اليوم ثمانية من رجالها فإذا هي فاطمة بنت يزيد بن السكن فقد قتل بين يديه أبوها وزوجها وولداها وأخواها وعمها وعم أبيها فلما نظرت في وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله كل مصيبة بعد رؤيتك جلل فعرفت أنه يستحق أكثر من هذا وأن ينصر بأكثر من هذا ولو كان لها من الرجال أضعاف هؤلاء كانوا أيضا قدموا أرواحهم فداءا لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نصرة له ودفاعا عنه.

• وقد اقتفى الناس سير الصحابة الصالحين في نصرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فكانت أيام الناس الخالدة في نصرة الإسلام في مشارق الأرض ومغاربها فتحت فيها الأمصار وهزمت الأمم ودخل فيها الناس في دين الله أفواجا ورد فيها الطاغون المعتدون وكسرت شوكة كل من يريد فتنة الناس عن دين الله، فقوتلوا جميعا على المحجة وعلى طريق الحق.

• وقد قامت الأمة الإسلامية في جميع العصور بالجهاد في سبيل الله وقياما لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنصرة، وكلما تقاعست الأمة عن هذه النصرة كلما أتتها الهزائم وانتصر أعداؤها عليها وذلك عندما تقع المخالفات الشرعية لأوامر الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وتلك عقوبة لمن خالف أمره تعالى.

هذه جملة مقتطفات موجزة من محاضرة الشيخ في هذا الموضوع، وللاستماع لها كاملة اضغط هنا
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew lectures to the Women's Association on: "Supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace".

His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture entitled "Supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace"

at the Ibn ʿAbbas Institute in the centre of the capital, Nouakchott, on the evening of yesterday, Monday 04-07-2011. It is a lecture that comes within the programme of the women's camp held by the Women's Association for Education and Culture on the Institute's premises. In this lecture the Sheikh took up the noble qualities of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and moving episodes of the Companions' support of him, may God be pleased with them. He mentioned that the measure of our love for him and of our reverence for the upright religion he brought is the measure of the support given to him and of the level of sacrifice in the cause of raising high the word of God Almighty. We mention the following of that in summary:

• God, glorified and exalted, chose Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, for His message with a choosing that preceded his creation; He selected him from among the prophets for His message, singled him out with the Night Journey and the Ascension, and raised him to a high station at the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary.

• And He honoured him among all creatures with the Greatest Intercession, from which the prophets of firm resolve among the messengers excused themselves, and said to him: "Intercede and you will be granted intercession; ask and you will be given…" God likewise singled him out with al-Wasīlah, which is a rank in Paradise that befits none but one man alone, and that is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.

• And He singled him out by making him a witness over all creatures: the messengers are God's witnesses over mankind, and the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, is a witness over them all. Among the conditions of this bearing witness is knowledge of the Sharia and deep understanding of the religion.

• And He honoured him by making him the one with the most followers on the Day of Resurrection. The prophets were shown to him on the Day of Resurrection, and he would see the prophet with a band of men with him, and the prophet with a small band, and the prophet with a single man, and the prophet with two men, and the prophet with no one with him at all — until he saw a great multitude and said: this is my community. It was said: this is Moses and his community; but look to the horizon. So he looked, and there was a great multitude that had filled the horizon, and it was said: this is your community, and with them are seventy thousand who will enter Paradise without reckoning and without punishment.

• And He honoured him on the Day of Resurrection with the banner bound for him on that Day: in his right hand is the Banner of Praise, which he raises, and beneath this banner the prophets and their communities and the righteous of every community enter. His own community comes with radiant faces and limbs; he knows them from among the communities, and they are called by his name: {On the day when We shall call every people by their leader — then whoever is given his record in his right hand, those will read their record and will not be wronged by so much as the thread of a date stone} (verse 71, al-Isrāʾ).

• And He honoured him likewise by sealing with him the message to the people of the earth, as an announcement that the true religion is what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought; for all the other religions were a preparation for this complete religion.

• And He honoured him likewise by making his community the best community brought forth for mankind: {And thus We have made you a middlemost community, so that you may be witnesses over mankind and the Messenger may be a witness over you} (part of verse 142 of Sūrat al-Baqarah).

• And He honoured him by making the scholars of his community like the prophets of the Children of Israel in rank, for the Children of Israel were governed by their prophets; so God made the scholars his heirs, and they govern his community as the prophets used to govern the Children of Israel. And God has undertaken for him that at the head of every hundred years He will raise up from this community one who will renew for it the matter of its religion.

• And likewise He honoured him by lifting hardship (ḥaraj) from his community, in sum and in detail. God Almighty said: {And He has laid upon you no hardship in religion — the creed of your father Abraham. He named you Muslims before} (part of verse 78 of Sūrat al-Ḥajj).

• When God, glorified and exalted, called us to support Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, He set before us the example of the disciples, when God sent Jesus and he called them to support him, and the Children of Israel divided into two parties and two groups, between those who held Jesus to be truthful and those who denied him. God Almighty said: {O you who believe, be helpers of God, as Jesus son of Mary said to the disciples: who are my helpers unto God? The disciples said: we are the helpers of God. So a group of the Children of Israel believed and a group disbelieved; and We supported those who believed against their enemy, and they became the ones prevailing} (verse 14, Sūrat al-Ṣaff).

• Among the moving episodes from the time of the Companions is that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the battle of Uhud and the people received him at the Mosque of al-Mustarah, he saw a woman whom the men were keeping away from him, and he said: let her be, for eight of her menfolk were killed before me today. And she was Fatimah bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan: her father, her husband, her two sons, her two brothers, her paternal uncle and her father's paternal uncle had been killed before him. When she looked into the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, she said: may my father and my mother be your ransom, O Messenger of God — every affliction after the sight of you is a light thing. So she knew that he deserved more than this, and to be supported with more than this; and had she had many times these men of hers, they too would have offered up their souls as a ransom for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in support of him and in his defence.

• And people followed the way of the righteous Companions in supporting the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and so there were the abiding days of the people in support of Islam in the east and the west of the earth, in which the great cities were opened and nations were defeated, and in which people entered into God's religion in throngs, and the tyrannical aggressors were repelled, and the strength was broken of everyone who sought to turn people away from God's religion by trial; and they were all fought on the clear road and on the path of truth.

• And in every age the Islamic community has undertaken the struggle in the cause of God (jihād), and has stood by the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in support of him. Whenever the community has held back from this support, defeats have come upon it and its enemies have prevailed over it — and that is when breaches of the Sharia occur against the commands of God and of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace; and that is a punishment for whoever contravenes the command of God Almighty.

These are a set of brief extracts from the Sheikh's lecture on this subject.

flags.arabic: (وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَاكُمْ أُمَّةً وَسَطاً …)(من الآية 142 من سورة البقرة)
flags.context: وشرفه كذلك بأن جعل أمته خير أمة أخرجت للناس
options: reproduce the source's locator as given (verse 142) and flag the error
flags.note: Two defects in one sentence, neither corrected. First, the locator is wrong: the verse quoted is Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:143, not 2:142. Second, the sentence introduces the quotation with the phrase خير أمة أخرجت للناس, which is from Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:110 and is not in the verse actually quoted; the verse quoted speaks of a middlemost community (ummah wasaṭ), which is a different claim. The English keeps both as the source has them. Style guide section 11 forbids silent repair.

flags.arabic: فقد عُرض عليه الأنبياء يوم القيامة
flags.context: وشرفه بأن جعله أكثر الرسل تابعا يوم القيامة؛ فقد عُرض عليه الأنبياء يوم القيامة
options: translate as given ('on the Day of Resurrection') and flag
read as a slip for the showing of the communities during the Night Journey and render accordingly
flags.note: In the well-known report the communities are shown to the Prophet during his lifetime, not on the Day of Resurrection; and the sentence has يوم القيامة twice over in a way that reads as a summariser's slip rather than a considered claim. Translated exactly as it stands and flagged; the English must not quietly relocate the event, and a reviewing scholar should check this against the audio before it is displayed.

flags.context: وقد قامت الأمة الإسلامية في جميع العصور بالجهاد في سبيل الله وقياما لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنصرة
options: the struggle in the cause of God (jihād)
striving in the cause of God (jihād)
jihad in the cause of God
flags.note: The house rule is plain English with the Arabic bracketed, so 'jihad' cannot stand alone as the English. The context here is unambiguously military — it follows a sentence about cities opened, nations defeated and aggressors repelled — so option 2 would soften it, which section 6 forbids, while leaving the loaded English word bare would let a reader supply a meaning the Arabic does not carry. 'Holy war' is not what the Arabic says and is not offered. The corpus needs one fixed rendering for جهاد, decided centrally.

flags.arabic: فكانت أيام الناس الخالدة في نصرة الإسلام … فتحت فيها الأمصار وهزمت الأمم … فقوتلوا جميعا على المحجة وعلى طريق الحق / وقد قامت الأمة الإسلامية في جميع العصور بالجهاد في سبيل الله
flags.context: the last two bullets of the record
options: translate faithfully and hold for an editorial decision
flags.note: Style guide section 12 — editorial_review. These two bullets celebrate the early conquests and then state that in every age the community has undertaken armed struggle, and that defeat follows when it holds back. In Arabic, in a lecture on love of the Prophet, this is a conventional historical and homiletic passage. Read in English, out of context, and in a summary that supplies none of the qualifications a jurist would attach, it can be taken for a contemporary exhortation. It is not softened and not strengthened here. Whether and how to publish belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office; the translator does not resolve it.

flags.arabic: فإذا هي فاطمة بنت يزيد بن السكن
flags.context: the story of the woman at the Mosque of al-Mustarah after Uhud
options: keep the name exactly as the source gives it
note the more commonly cited names for this woman
flags.note: The woman in the best-known versions of this report is usually named otherwise, and the number and relationship of her dead differ between versions. The source's name and its list of eight are reproduced without alteration. Flagged so that a reviewing scholar can check the narration against the audio before the record is displayed; the translator must not substitute a version he happens to know.

flags.arabic: هذه جملة مقتطفات موجزة من محاضرة الشيخ في هذا الموضوع، وللاستماع لها كاملة اضغط هنا
flags.context: the closing sentence, and the status of the whole record
options: render with an excerpt banner and a link to the recording, never as a text by the Sheikh
flags.note: critical_for_display. The record states in its own closing sentence that it is a set of brief extracts and that the lecture itself is the audio at /index.php/dawa/dawa.html?view=media&id=1463. The bullets are the news desk's compression, not the Sheikh's wording, and the two most exposed of them are the two at the end.

translator_notes: This is a news report, and an avowedly abridged one. Everything attributed to the Sheikh arrives at second hand and in summary.
The CMS timestamp is a bulk-upload date and is not evidence of when the report was written. The body dates the lecture to the evening of Monday 4 July 2011, which is better evidence.

The first line of the body repeats the record's own title verbatim, with a small difference in spacing. It is a CMS duplication rather than part of the report, but it is preserved in body_ar and rendered in body_en because the style guide forbids skipping a paragraph. The site should suppress it in display.
The second and third paragraphs of body_ar are one sentence broken across a line break in the source, and are rendered here as the single sentence they are; the break is preserved in body_ar.
Qur'anic renderings here are interpretive and are not a substitute for the Arabic. Locators are given exactly in the form the source gives them, including the erroneous one flagged above.
No collection and no grading is given for the two prophetic reports quoted ('Intercede and you will be granted intercession…' and the showing of the communities), so the English supplies neither.

No ruling words occur in this record, so the five-rulings mapping of style guide section 3 is not engaged. الواجب does not appear; حرج is rendered 'hardship' in its ordinary sense and is not the technical mashaqqah of the glossary.
The source's closing clause 'to listen to it in full, click here' is the site's navigation furniture; preserved in body_ar, recorded in source_download_link, omitted from body_en.
